data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word 'Ramz', meaning 'night' or 'moon'. Ramzah is a beautiful and meaningful name for a baby girl. The name Ramzah carries the meaning “Night, Moon” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, English. Parents who choose Ramzah usually hope their child will grow to embody night, moon and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the peace and tranquility of the night and the illumination of the moon. A perfect name for a child who embodies these qualities.
data.etymology: Ramzah belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Night, Moon.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ramzah total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.
data.cultural_impact: Ramadan, referred to as Ramzah in some regions, is the holiest month in the Islamic calendar. During this time, practice of the Islamic fast called Sawm, where Muslims abstain from food, drink, or sexual activity from dawn until sunset, is observed. The cultural significance of Ramzah lies in the communal experience it fosters, where families and communities come together to share meals and strengthen bonds. This month is also characterized by acts of charity, self-reflection and devotion.
data.spiritual_significance: In terms of spiritual significance, Ramzah is a time for Muslims to purify their souls, seek forgiveness for past sins, and redirect their actions towards the path of righteousness. The practice of the fast itself symbolizes self-control, discipline, and selflessness, all essential Islamic virtues. Jenazah, the Arabic word for funeral, is derived from the same root as 'Ramz' and carries a similar meaning of 'restraining', reflecting the connection between spiritual and physical self-control. May a child blessed with the name of Ramzah grow up to embody these lofty virtues.
